fixes.explanation: Egypt isn't on the guest list for this view, friend. The LORD shows Moses the land, from Gilead as far as Dan, and all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea (Deuteronomy 34:1-2). Then He says, "This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob…" (Deuteronomy 34:4). That's what Moses is looking at, a promise, not a way back.

This one is true, baker. The text says no prophet performed "…all the mighty acts of power and awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel." (Deuteronomy 34:12) Moses did those deeds in the sight of all Israel, so the whole nation saw them. Verse 11 adds the signs and wonders the LORD sent Moses to do in Egypt, to Pharaoh, his officials and all his land (Deuteronomy 34:11).

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The passage does not say that Egypt was out of Moses’ view or behind him. It says what land the LORD showed him, not everything he could or could not see.

The explanation says the preceding verse makes the same point about all Israel seeing the signs and wonders in Egypt. Verse 11 says they were done to Pharaoh, his officials, and his land; it does not say all Israel saw them.
